'''Nir Friedman''' ({{Langx|he|ניר פרידמן}}; born 1967) is an Israeli [[professor]] of [[computer science]] and [[biology]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Nir Friedman |url=http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~nir/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060103152702/http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~nir/ |archive-date=2006-01-03 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.cs.huji.ac.il}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Nir Friedman’s Lab |url=http://systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il/Friedmans_Lab/Home.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214095021/http://systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il/Friedmans_Lab/Home.html |archive-date=2011-12-14 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il |language=en}}</ref>

His research combines [[machine learning]] and [[statistical learning|statistical learning]] with [[systems biology]], specifically in the fields of [[gene regulation|gene regulation]], [[transcription (genetics)|transcription]] and [[chromatin]].

==Education and research==
Friedman earned his BSc degree from [[Tel Aviv University]] (1987) and his MSc from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (1992).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Friedman |first=Nir |title=Curriculum Vitae—Nir Friedman |url=http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~nir/resume.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060708143806/http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~nir/resume.pdf |archive-date=2006-07-08 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.cs.huji.ac.il}}</ref> In 1997, he completed his Ph.D. at [[Stanford]] under the supervision of [[Joseph Halpern]], in the field of [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-robotics.stanford.edu/~nir/Abstracts/Thesis.html |title=Modeling Beliefs in Dynamic Systems |access-date=October 22, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425083007/http://www-robotics.stanford.edu/~nir/Abstracts/Thesis.html |archive-date=April 25, 2012 |date=1997|last=Friedman|first=N.}}</ref>

After some [[postdoctoral]] work at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], he accepted a faculty position at the School of Computer Science,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cs.huji.ac.il|title=The Rachel and Selim Benin School of Computer Science and Engineering|website=Cs.huji.ac.il|access-date=25 May 2016}}</ref> the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

His highly cited research<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=nir+friedman|title=nir friedman - Google Scholar|website=Scholar.google.com|access-date=25 May More recent works focus on [[Graphical model|Probabilistic Graphical Models]], reconstructing [[Gene regulatory network|Regulatory Networks]], [[Genetic interactions|Genetic Interactions]], and the role of [[Chromatin]] in Transcriptional Regulation (with [[Oliver J. Rando|Oliver Rando]])<ref name=":0" />

In 2009, Friedman and [[Daphne Koller|Koller]] published a textbook on [[Graphical model|Probabilistic Graphical Models]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Daphne Koller and Nir Friedman|title=Probabilistic Graphical Models|publisher=MIT Press |year=2009|isbn=978-0-262-01319-2}}</ref> Later that year, he joined the Institute of Life Sciences,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bio.huji.ac.il/eng|title=The Alexander Silberman Institute of Life Sciences|website=Bio.huji.ac.il|access-date=2016-05-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426002630/http://bio.huji.ac.il/eng/|archive-date=2016-04-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> and opened an experimental lab where he uses advanced robotic tools to study transcriptional regulation in the yeast [[Saccharomyces cerevisiae]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robotic Facility |url=http://systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il/Friedmans_Lab/Robotic_Facility.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425083518/http://systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il/Friedmans_Lab/Robotic_Facility.html |archive-date=2012-04-25 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=systemsbio.cs.huji.ac.il |language=en}}</ref>
